newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply up as peso weakens.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply up as peso weakens.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates climbed 180 basis points to end at 21 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers said investors sold paper in the secondary market to switch to dollars, which were still attractively priced in early trade.
"As the dollar was so cheap, it obviously triggered demand and that put rates under pressure," a fixed-income analyst said.
Demand for dollars led to a run on the peso, which pushed rates up higher, analysts said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended 6.6 centavos weaker at 7.9150/7.9250 per dollar.
Dealers said recent central bank operations to drain liquidity from the market had also added to pressures on secondary rates. Banco de Mexico drained 564 million pesos from the market on Tuesday.
Dealers said pressure on the peso and on secondary market rates led them to forecast gains in primary interest rates, rather than the cuts they had expected on Monday.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders showed they forecast the central bank would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average 19.36 percent. This would be a rise of 99 basis points since last week's auction.
The central bank was expected to release auction results at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 170 basis points at 21.50 percent.
Liquidity of 673 million pesos was due to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
